texas-football.summary: Texas rallied past Ohio State 24-23. Against UTSA, the next step is making the offense work before a comeback becomes necessary: establish the running game, give Manning clear reads, and keep the defense closing drives.

items.headline: Texas ran for 67 yards in the fourth quarter
items.tldr: Watch whether the blocking and backfield can produce that control early against UTSA. Useful gains would keep the passing game out of rescue mode.

items.headline: Sarkisian gave no return date for Townsend’s knee injury
items.tldr: Keep Townsend’s status separate from the available tight-end options. Terry also missed Ohio State after a foot injury in warmups; watch for the next update on both.

items.headline: Texas shut Ohio State out in the fourth quarter
items.tldr: Watch the coverage discipline after halftime carry into the opening series. Getting off the field would give the offense room to settle.

items.headline: UTSA converted two fourth downs on its winning drive
items.tldr: Prepare for an opponent willing to extend possessions. Watch McCown’s keeper as well as the short pass when Texas needs one more stop.

items.headline: DKR’s map locates gates, water stations and first aid
items.tldr: Pick your entrance before leaving for the stadium. Save the map alongside your ticket so it is easy to find on arrival.

lead.headline: Start with the running game.
lead.body: Carry the late-game blocking into the opening drives. Steady gains would make Manning’s reads simpler and keep Texas from needing another rescue.

matchup.question: What should Texas carry into UTSA?
matchup.answer: Build drives with the running backs, use the tight end when the outside throw is covered, and defend through fourth down.

utah-state-football.summary: Utah State fell 16-14 at Washington with Brosterhous making his first start. Utah is next. The defense kept the game close, but the offense needs designed runs that work and fewer possessions ending with the ball in opposing hands.

items.headline: Brosterhous started at Washington in place of Hillstead
items.tldr: Watch this week’s quarterback announcement before assuming the same starter for Utah.

items.headline: Seven of eight running-back carries failed to gain yards
items.tldr: Watch whether the blocks create a path for the backs. The offense needs dependable designed runs alongside the quarterback’s scrambles.

items.headline: Utah State allowed one touchdown at Washington
items.tldr: Repeat those stops against Utah.

items.headline: Utah beat Arkansas 43-10 before the rivalry game
items.tldr: Watch the quarterback both in the pocket and on keepers. Losing track of the back or tight end can turn containment into an open passing lane.

items.headline: Rice-Eccles scans tickets before security screening
items.tldr: Download your ticket into your phone’s wallet before arrival. Utah’s entry guide also points to no-bag lanes at the main gates.

lead.headline: Give the backs somewhere to go.
lead.body: Watch the designed runs before judging the offense by a scramble or a deep completion. Useful gains would make the next passing down less predictable.

matchup.question: What would give Utah State a chance at Utah?
matchup.answer: Create space for the running backs, protect the ball, and make the opposing quarterback finish drives through tight coverage.

ohio-state-football.summary: Ohio State lost 24-23 at Texas after its fourth-quarter lead disappeared. Kent State is next. Watch whether the offense can keep moving beyond its first receiving option and whether the defensive front can finish a possession.

items.headline: Day singled out negative plays in the red zone
items.tldr: Watch the edge blocking and pocket protection near the goal line. Keeping the next play manageable is the first step toward finishing drives.

items.headline: Smith drew 15 targets; the other wideouts caught two passes
items.tldr: Watch the second read and the routes underneath. Keeping more receivers involved would make it harder to stall the offense by covering Smith.

items.headline: Timmons forced and recovered a fumble on the opening snap
items.tldr: Watch his tackling and ball awareness continue through a full possession. The early takeaway is useful evidence of what he can contribute.

items.headline: Hawkins made three field goals, then missed from 45 yards
items.tldr: Watch the full kicking operation when a drive stalls. Points from those possessions can decide whether a late defensive stop is enough.

items.headline: Kent State’s DeShields ran for two touchdowns against Wofford
items.tldr: The quarterback is another player the run defense must account for. Watch the edge and open-field tackling when he leaves the pocket.

lead.headline: Keep the next drive alive.
lead.body: Watch for a clean answer when the first receiver is covered. Moving the chains would let the defense recover and make a lead easier to protect.

matchup.question: What would show progress against Kent State?
matchup.answer: Convert manageable third downs, find receivers beyond the first read, and pressure the quarterback without opening a running lane.

lsu-football.summary: LSU beat Louisiana Tech 45-14 despite four first-half turnovers. The trip to Ole Miss makes ball security the priority. Watch Leavitt’s decisions near the goal line and whether the defensive pressure travels to Oxford.

items.headline: Leavitt threw three interceptions, two in the red zone
items.tldr: Watch the decision when the first scoring option is covered. Keeping a possession alive matters more than forcing a touchdown throw.

items.headline: Umanmielen recorded three sacks against Louisiana Tech
items.tldr: Watch whether the defensive front can disrupt the pocket while keeping its lanes. A free scramble can undo otherwise effective pressure.

items.headline: Chambliss completed 23 of 26 passes against Charlotte
items.tldr: Watch the underneath coverage as closely as the pass rush. Making the quarterback hold the ball would give pressure time to arrive.

items.headline: Construction changes the route around The Grove
items.tldr: Check the revised pickup and dropoff directions before driving into Oxford. Plan the approach to campus as well as the parking spot.

items.headline: Kiffin wants LSU focused on preparation for his Oxford return
items.tldr: Watch the communication before the snap and the response after a bad play. Keeping attention on the next assignment is the useful test of that message.

lead.headline: Keep the ball in Oxford.
lead.body: Watch Leavitt’s decisions when space gets tight. A throw away can preserve a scoring chance; a forced pass can give the opponent the next possession.

matchup.question: What matters most at Ole Miss?
matchup.answer: Protect the ball near the goal line, make the opposing quarterback work past his first read, and keep defensive pressure under control.
